Stage Setup, Breathing Exercise & Welcome

( Walk onto the stage with a warm, confident smile. Step up to your brewing station and make direct eye contact with each judge.)
Welcome & Shared Breathing


Hello judges! I’m Tuấn from Da Nang, a beautiful coastal city, where life reminds us every day to slow down and enjoy the present moment
So I was brewing coffee as a hobby. In those quiet moment, I simply feel the enjoyment
And you can see that enjoyment across every stage in the world of coffee: 
The farmers feel enjoy their harvest, 
Roasters feel enjoy unlocking flavors, 
and as a barista, I feel the same when brewing this cup for you today.

However, five years in coffee taught me that:  the personal enjoyment is only half the story. Real enjoy happens when we can transfer the joy from "me" to "us"

To share that enjoyment to you, I crafted a routine focused on three things: 
First : the right coffee,
Second : the right tools,
And the third :  an simple recipe
 
(Option 2:  To bring it from me to us, today I will create a bridge that connect the enjoyment from me to it)

<div class="transclusion internal-embed is-loaded"><div class="markdown-embed">




The first thing: this is the flavors I truly enjoy
Today I will blend two Gesha from Panama:
First : 7 gram of Panama Gesha from [[VNBRC26/BEAN SELECTION/Janson\|Janson]] family ,  for its complex of flavors and sweetness. It is Anaerobic Natural that was 48 hours anaerobic fermentation, then slow dry with sun combine mechanical drum drying
Second : 7 gram of Panama Gesha, from [[VNBRC26/BEAN SELECTION/Alto Bambito\|Alto Bambito]], for the complex acidity and mouthfeel for my final cup. This is A classic honey process by Arturo Guerra.

Both coffees are grown at around 2000 meters above sea level. With cool night time temperatures, the coffee cherries underdo a slower maturation. This allow the cherries to produce more sugars, resulting a stone fruits complex sweetness that we will taste later.

![3. Bean selection-1786875507533.webp](/img/user/Attachments/3.%20Bean%20selection-1786875507533.webp)



</div></div>



<div class="transclusion internal-embed is-loaded"><div class="markdown-embed">





These coffees were roasted exactly two weeks ago, now my coffee is at their absolute peak flavors  
With Stronghold roaster, by its a hybrid heat transfer including: induction, convection and radiation, help my favorite flavors unlocked evenly.
To make sure all the flavors in this blend shine through, I roast them to with 13% development time. This help the extraction stays balanced.

</div></div>



<div class="transclusion internal-embed is-loaded"><div class="markdown-embed">




##### solo spin: less workflow, enjoying more

I talked about the first things - my favorite coffee.
Now lets move to second thing : To choose my favorite dripper
I choose this dripper because its simple design and interesting workflow,
( Put the second card on the board )
( then get a solo spin to show for judges to see inside out )

In my hand is the dripper that I enjoy so much: The Solo Spin
This is the Solo body: Flat bottom with 40 degree straight wall, big open base, help increase the speed of drainage, reserve the clarity of flavors.
Also the Tri-tan material, work as a natural seal to the coffee bed, maintain the temperature in the extraction process.
This is the Spin base : You can simply Spin this button to change between Percolation, Immersion, or hybrid extraction.

I have a Solo, I have a Spin
Boom 
The Solo Spin
What I have now is the dripper which drain fast, consistent to temperature, and easy to change between percolation and immersion.


</div></div>



<div class="transclusion internal-embed is-loaded"><div class="markdown-embed">





this is hiflux fast filter. I choose it because of 2 reason:
- 1. It drains fast, enough to bring all flavors out as I expected, without clogging even if I use small grind size
- 2. It provides better mouthfeel. Because this Lyocell material will traps bitter, astringent and larger fines, while allowing positive ultra-fines (<20 μm) and natural coffee lipids to pass through, increase mouthfeel and clarity.

</div></div>



<div class="transclusion internal-embed is-loaded"><div class="markdown-embed">




With my dripper and Paper filter setup, I choose to grind coffee at 700 microns, enough to extract my flavors with high flowrate, while keep the clearer cup and the smooth mouthfeel.

</div></div>



<div class="transclusion internal-embed is-loaded"><div class="markdown-embed">





For water : I simply use 35ppm natural mineral water, to boost the extraction while keep the origin flavors bright and intense.
Today I use water at 2 different temperature : 94 then 80 degree celcius - which I will tell you more details later.

</div></div>



<div class="transclusion internal-embed is-loaded"><div class="markdown-embed">





Today I use a very simple recipe, easy to replicate . 
My recipe divide into 2 phases, both 2 phases is the immersion method:
-  I use 14 gram of coffee, with 220 gram water. #ratio is 1:15. The right #ratio to achieve the balance between flavor and mouthfeel for my blend.
- The first phase: 100 gram of water at 94 celsius degree, spiral pattern of pouring. Total time of the this phase is 1 minute and 15 second, with 100 gram of water and long time of blooming.
- This helps coffee powder get saturated, and the extraction process slowly - smooth happen, keep the flavors slowly transfer from the coffee particle out to my coffee liquid
- At 1 minutes and 20 second, i will #spin this button at full level to let all the liquid flow down. the drawn time is around 15 seconds. 
- The second phase: I replicate the first phase, but with a 120 gram water at 85 degree celsius : 
- The higher volume and lower temperature will help the extraction still going, bring out more sweetness and structure for final cup, but reduce the negative flavors, which usually appear at the final phase of extraction.


</div></div>



<div class="transclusion internal-embed is-loaded"><div class="markdown-embed">




Now, my judges, you can please spend time to take note my flavor description:

Aroma ( hot stage ):

As you gently swirl your vessel, you will find a medium-high intensity aroma dominated by fresh jasmine blossom, sweet bergamot, and a hint of warm honey

For <mark style="background-color: #BBFABBA6;">flavor</mark>, it will be medium intensity.  
When it's hot, it's hibiscus and mandarin orange.  
And as it cools down, it will shift into apricot, red apple, and sugarcane.  

For the <mark style="background-color: #BBFABBA6;">aftertaste</mark>, it's medium intensity, long and lingering. 
When it's hot, it reminds me of mandarin orange.  
And as it cools down, it will become long and sweet like sugarcane.  

For the <mark style="background-color: #BBFABBA6;">acidity</mark>, it's medium intensity.  
When it's hot, it's vibrant and citric like orange.  
And as it cools down, it will become lively and malic like apricot and red apple.  

And for the <mark style="background-color: #BBFABBA6;">sweetness</mark>, it's medium intensity.  
When it's hot, it's fruity sweetness like orange.  
And as it cools down, it will become fruity sweetness like red apple and sugary, like sugarcane.  

And finally, for the <mark style="background-color: #BBFABBA6;">mouthfeel</mark>, it's medium intensity.
When it's hot, it's smooth.  
And as it cools down, it will become round and juicy.
(Developed through the gentle immersion of the effect of Hiflux #lyocell filter paper).

</div></div>
